accepted.title: The drama list
accepted.text: Teacher announces that our class gets to perform a funny play for Annual Day. You jump with joy because you love acting! But next to you, Ayaan frowns and looks at the floor. He really wanted the dance performance instead. What do you do?

options.text: Celebrate loudly and tell Ayaan plays are way better than dances
options.consequence: Ayaan looks annoyed and walks off to sit by the stage.

options.text: Quietly ask Ayaan if he is feeling upset about the dance
options.consequence: Ayaan sighs and nods, but he looks relieved that you noticed.

options.text: Ignore Ayaan's frown and start practising your lines
options.consequence: You have fun reading, but Ayaan stays silent for the rest of rehearsal.

hint.text: Why might Ayaan feel differently from you about the same announcement?

grade.rationale: Option B demonstrates clear empathy (social awareness) and supportive communication (relationship skills) by tuning into a classmate's non-verbal cues. Option A dismisses Ayaan's feelings, while Option C lacks care for a friend. Balancing personal excitement with concern for a peer is a realistic challenge for 8-10 year olds.

Consequences are grounded and realistic; acknowledging Ayaan's feelings offers relief without falsely erasing his disappointment.

accepted.title: Turns at carrom
accepted.text: Your cousins are playing carrom at your house. Gurpreet speaks with a stammer. A cousin giggles and says Gurpreet is too slow to play. Gurpreet looks down and steps back from the board. What do you do?

options.text: Keep playing so the match does not stop
options.consequence: The game goes on, but Gurpreet sits alone by the wall.

options.text: Tell your cousin calmly that everyone gets their turn
options.consequence: Your cousin stops giggling and passes the striker to Gurpreet.

options.text: Ask Gurpreet to be your carrom partner
options.consequence: Gurpreet smiles, sits beside you, and gets ready to play.

options.text: Tell Chachi that Gurpreet is being left out
options.consequence: Chachi comes over and helps make sure every cousin gets an equal turn.

hint.text: How might Gurpreet feel when others make fun of his speech?

grade.rationale: Option B and Option C both demonstrate strong empathy and inclusion. Calmly reminding others of fairness or directly inviting Gurpreet to join demonstrates high social awareness and relationship skills, whereas ignoring the situation leaves a peer hurt.

accepted.title: After the team list
accepted.text: At football practice, Coach announces the match team. Harsh isn't on the list. Harsh laughs loudly and shrugs. "Who cares anyway? Saturday matches are boring." But you notice his hands trembling as he zips his kit bag. What do you do?

options.text: Laugh along and agree that weekend matches are totally boring
options.consequence: Harsh stops laughing, turns away quickly, and sits alone on the bench.

options.text: Walk with him to the water tap and quietly say, "Tough luck, Harsh. You played well."
options.consequence: Harsh looks relieved that someone noticed, and he quietly admits he feels sad.

options.text: Say loudly in front of the others, "Stop faking, Harsh, you're actually crying"
options.consequence: Harsh's face goes red with embarrassment and he snaps at you to leave him alone.

options.text: Give him space right now, but walk home together after practice
options.consequence: Once away from the crowd, Harsh opens up about how much he wanted to play.

hint.text: Why might someone laugh when something disappointing happens?

grade.rationale: Recognising Harsh's hidden disappointment requires social awareness. Option B is the best response because it offers quiet, private validation without calling public attention to his embarrassment.

reasons: Cleanly and accurately captures the 'hidden feelings' construct.
Consequences are realistic, gentle, and psychologically believable for 8-10 year olds.
Options B and D offer realistic, empathetic pathways without preaching.

showNotPreach.note: The outcomes show social cause and effect without moralizing commentary.

accepted.title: Locked outside
accepted.text: Our class group chat has a strict rule set by Sharma Sir: no messages after 8 PM, or you get removed and given detention. At 9:15 PM, Nikhil posts: 'Please help, I'm stuck outside the coaching centre in heavy rain, the gate locked, and my battery is at 2%.' The class monitor quickly types, 'Rules are rules, Nikhil. Delete this or Sir will punish us all.' What do you do?

options.text: Stay quiet so I do not get into trouble for breaking the chat rule
options.consequence: Nikhil's status goes offline, and he remains stuck alone in the rain.

options.text: Call Sharma Sir directly to explain that Nikhil is stranded and needs help
options.consequence: Sharma Sir contacts the building security guard immediately to let Nikhil wait inside safely.

options.text: Reply in the group chat and argue with the monitor for being selfish
options.consequence: A heated argument begins on the chat while Nikhil's battery completely runs out.

options.text: Send Nikhil a private message wishing him luck so I do not break the group rule
options.consequence: Nikhil's screen goes black before he can read it, leaving him without assistance.

hint.text: Which matters more right now: avoiding a detention or making sure Nikhil is safe?

grade.rationale: This scenario forces students to weigh personal safety against strict rule compliance. Calling the teacher directly addresses the real-world emergency responsibly without starting an argument in the group chat.

reasons: Accurately captures the research construct of prioritizing personal safety over strict rule compliance.

accepted.title: The museum argument
accepted.text: During our class trip to the science museum, Harsh and Aarav storm over to me. Harsh says Aarav dragged his feet at the dinosaur hall and ruined their chance to see the planetarium show. Aarav snaps back that Harsh hurried everyone through without looking at anything. Harsh demands, "Tell him he ruined the group plan!" Aarav insists, "Tell him he was being bossy!" Both want me to back them up. What do you do?

options.text: Agree with Harsh, because keeping to the museum schedule was the plan
options.consequence: Harsh nods, but Aarav feels unheard and walks off alone to the gift shop.

options.text: Say, "Harsh was worried about missing the show, and Aarav wanted time to see the exhibits. Can we check the show timings together?"
options.consequence: Both pause, realising what the other wanted, and check the timetable for the afternoon show.

options.text: Walk away to another exhibit so I do not have to pick a side
options.consequence: They continue arguing by the hall entrance until a teacher steps in to separate them.

options.text: Quietly tell Aarav later that Harsh was being unfair to him
options.consequence: Aarav feels supported, but the cold silence between him and Harsh lasts the entire bus ride home.

hint.text: What was each friend trying to achieve, and is there a way both can be heard?

grade.rationale: Option B demonstrates high social awareness by recognizing both perspectives and strong relationship skills by mediating neutrally. Navigating peer pressure to take sides is challenging for this age group.

reasons: Accurately models the research construct of third-party conflict mediation without taking sides.
Consequences are grounded, realistic, and avoid magical resolutions.
Language and setting are authentic for middle-school children in India.

accepted.title: Between two desks
accepted.text: During zero period, Kavya and Diya argue over who should represent the class in the inter-school quiz. Kavya pulls you aside, saying Diya already got to go last month. options.text: Side with Kavya so that someone new gets a turn

options.text: Suggest the three of us talk it through together so both can explain their points calmly
options.consequence: It takes patience, but both realise they each have a fair point to discuss with the teacher.

options.text: Tell Diya what Kavya whispered about her
options.consequence: The argument turns into a loud shouting match right before the teacher walks in.

options.text: Say I have nothing to do with this and walk out to the corridor

hint.text: What might the situation look like if you stepped back and saw both of their reasons?

accepted.title: Candlelight ludo
accepted.text: The power goes out, so you and Neha play ludo by candlelight. You win three games in a row. Neha laughs loudly and says, "Winning is boring anyway!" But her fingers twist her dupatta tightly, and her voice shakes. What do you do?

options.text: Laugh and say, "You're only saying that because you lost!"
options.consequence: Neha stops laughing, folds her arms tightly, and looks down at the floor.

options.text: Suggest switching to telling ghost stories so neither of you has to win or lose
options.consequence: Neha lets go of her dupatta and excitedly starts the first spooky story.

options.text: Quietly ask if she is actually upset about the games
options.consequence: Neha looks down in the candlelight, then admits losing three times felt bad.

hint.text: Neha is laughing, but what are her hands and voice showing?

grade.rationale: Noticing the tension between Neha's words and her physical cues requires social awareness. Option B tactfully protects Neha's feelings by shifting to a non-competitive activity, while Option C shows direct empathy. Option A gloats and damages the relationship.

Culturally grounded and realistic scenario for children in India.

accepted.title: Torn chart in the library
accepted.text: In the quiet school library, you are finishing your history timeline. Imran rushes past your table carrying a towering stack of encyclopaedias. His heavy bag knocks your chart to the floor, tearing a corner. Imran keeps hurrying towards the issue desk without looking back. Your hard work is torn, and you wonder if he ignored it on purpose after yesterday's disagreement. What do you do?

options.text: Knock his notebook off the desk when you walk past to get even
options.consequence: Imran glares at you, a librarian shushes both of you, and the tension between you grows.

options.text: Go over quietly and ask him if he realised his bag caught your chart
options.consequence: Imran looks mortified—the tall stack blocked his view. He apologises and helps tape the tear.

options.text: Give him the benefit of the doubt, pick up the sheet, and fix the tear yourself
options.consequence: You finish mending your work in peace, avoiding an argument, though you still wonder what happened.

options.text: Complain to the librarian that Imran damaged your project on purpose
options.consequence: The librarian tells you to resolve it outside, and Imran feels unfairly accused.

hint.text: Could there be a reason Imran didn't notice the chart fall?

Option B shows strong relationship skills through polite direct communication, while Option C highlights self-management and empathy by keeping calm and giving the benefit of the doubt. Consequences are natural, realistic, and avoid preachiness.

feelingsStayReal.note: Acknowledge the lingering uncertainty and sting of damaged work naturally.

accepted.title: The surprise trip

accepted.title: Broken diyas at the mela
accepted.text: At the society Diwali celebration, you just finished arranging painted clay diyas along the courtyard ledge. Chirag hurries past, his kurta sleeve brushing the ledge. Two diyas crash to the tiles and shatter. Chirag keeps walking toward the entrance without turning around. Your chest tightens with annoyance. What do you do?

options.text: Yell after him that he ruined my work on purpose
options.consequence: Nearby aunties turn to stare, and an uncomfortable silence falls over your corner of the courtyard.

options.text: Catch up to Chirag and ask if he realised what happened
options.consequence: Chirag turns around startled, holding medicine for his coughing dadi; he looks genuinely horrified and offers to sweep the pieces.

options.text: Shrug it off, assume the crowd was loud, and sweep the broken clay away
options.consequence: The walkway is safe again quickly, though a slight prickle of doubt lingers about why he did not look back.

options.text: Complain to the society committee uncle about Chirag's carelessness
options.consequence: The uncle sighs and asks if you spoke to Chirag directly before reporting him.

hint.text: Could someone be in a hurry without meaning to cause harm?

grade.rationale: Option B demonstrates strong relationship skills by directly communicating with Chirag without hostile assumptions. Option C also shows good self-management and social awareness by keeping calm and giving benefit of the doubt. Yelling (A) or telling an adult immediately (D) needlessly escalates minor accidents.

reasons: Accurately maps the 'Accident or on purpose?' construct with genuine ambiguity and believable innocent explanation.
Culturally grounded setting and realistic adolescent emotional responses without preaching.

feelingsStayReal.note: Names initial irritation clearly and honors the lingering prickle of doubt in option C.

showNotPreach.note: The consequences show the impact directly through character reactions without preaching.

accepted.title: Ranked Match Blame
accepted.text: During a ranked squad match, your team loses after a messy final round. Immediately, Thomas direct-messages you: "Imran ignored my ping and hid. Don't queue with him next round." options.text: Agree with Thomas and tell Imran he should have followed the team lead
options.consequence: Imran leaves the party feeling ganged up on, and Thomas expects you to keep backing him.

options.text: Secretly agree with Imran, but tell Thomas that Imran just had bad lag

options.text: Bring both onto group voice and point out that the chaos made it hard for either to see what the other was doing
options.consequence: Both pause, realising neither was trying to ruin the game, and agree to take a five-minute break.

options.text: Ignore both messages and queue up for a solo match instead
options.consequence: Both boys wonder why you went quiet, and the argument between them continues unaddressed.

hint.text: What was each friend trying to achieve during that chaotic round?

accepted.title: The silent bus
accepted.text: The school bus is stuck in a humid traffic jam. Two rows ahead, Simran is clutching her stomach, turning pale and sweating, clearly about to faint. Everyone is staring ahead, afraid of getting into trouble. What do you do?

options.text: Keep quiet and stay seated so I don't risk a discipline card
options.consequence: You avoid trouble, but Simran slumps forward against the seat, struggling alone.

options.text: Unbuckle my belt and rush over to Simran with my water bottle
options.consequence: The bus suddenly jolts forward, making you stumble into the aisle, and the attendant shouts in alarm.

options.text: Raise my hand and call out to the attendant, explaining that Simran is feeling very sick
options.consequence: The attendant frowns at the broken rule, but hurries over to help Simran the moment he sees her.

options.text: Whisper to the students in front of me to ask what we should do
options.consequence: The whispers cause a nervous buzz, but no one actually steps forward to help her.

hint.text: Why might an everyday rule need to be paused in this moment?

grade.rationale: This scenario presents a moral dilemma between obeying strict rules to avoid punishment and speaking up during a medical emergency. Option C is the most responsible choice because it alerts the adult supervisor immediately while maintaining physical safety by staying seated. Option A prioritizes self-preservation over empathy, while Option B creates safety risks on the bus.

reasons: Captures the construct faithfully with a realistic conflict between strict bus rules and classmate wellbeing.
Consequences are grounded and believable, showing safety hazards of rushing in a moving bus and bystander inertia.

accepted.title: Caught in the middle
accepted.text: On Sunday afternoon, your brother Vikram and sister Simran start arguing over the TV remote. Vikram says he needs to unwind after his mock exam, while Simran says he watched cricket all of yesterday. Both turn to you at once, demanding, "Tell them who's right!" What do you do?

options.text: Side with Vikram just so the shouting stops quickly
options.consequence: Simran leaves the room upset, and the silence in the hall feels tense.

options.text: Tell them, "Vikram is stressed from tests, but Simran waited all yesterday. Can you split the time?"
options.consequence: Both stop to think, realising why the other is frustrated, and agree to take turns.

options.text: Walk away to your room so you don't get dragged into it
options.consequence: The shouting gets louder until your mother comes in and switches the TV off.

options.text: Tell Simran that Vikram said she was being stubborn earlier
options.consequence: Simran becomes even more furious, and the argument turns into personal insults.

hint.text: What does this disagreement look like if you listen to both of their reasons?

grade.rationale: Option B demonstrates strong social awareness and relationship skills by validating both siblings' perspectives and suggesting a fair compromise. The other options either escalate the tension, pick a side out of convenience, or avoid helping constructively.

candidate.title: Deleted notes
candidate.text: You spent an hour typing out history revision notes and shared the PDF in the class group chat. Two minutes later, Simran, one of the group admins, deletes your message without leaving any explanation. Your face burns as you stare at the screen. What do you do?

options.text: Post in the group asking why Simran is being petty and deleting your hard work
options.consequence: The chat gets tense with people taking sides, and Simran temporarily mutes the group.

options.text: Message Simran privately to ask if there was a problem with the file
options.consequence: Simran replies saying the PDF preview was glitching into blank pages, and asks you to re-send.

options.text: Assume it was a technical glitch and re-post the file with a brief note
